decision: 007's 'mermaid render' premise was false: no mermaid lib exists (not vendored/dep/node_modules) and the Architecture page already renders a rich interactive swimlane SVG. Operator chose: NO mermaid vendor — (F001) regenerate the diff-able per-level .mmd levels in the build (cache-only, foreign-repo guarded) + (F002) breadcrumb cluster-zoom on the EXISTING SVG. Avoids a ~3MB dependency + redundancy with the shipped interactive render.

Operator refined 007: the architecture surface is an INTERACTIVE COMPONENT MAP, not a diagram-text renderer. Model = state → normalized graph/levels DATA → interactive SVG map → click→highlight upstream/downstream + dim unrelated + detail + drill-down, breadcrumb level path. Source of truth is the graph model {nodes,edges,levels,clusters,metadata,freshness}; .mmd is an OPTIONAL diffable export only. F001 re-pointed to emit the graph/level data (not mermaid); F002 = the interactive map behaviors on the existing SVG. Do NOT vendor mermaid.

Handoff named architecture_levels.cluster_key/write_levels as an existing seam to extend, but no such module existed (verified: only architecture_view_state.py). Real seams: (F001) build_view_state in architecture_view_state.py already emits nodes/edges/freshness/lanes/flows — added clusters[]+levels[] there (the render source of truth); (F002) the existing interactive swimlane SVG in dashboard/lib/architecture-logic.js + pages/architecture/architecture.js. Created architecture_levels.py NEW to own cluster_key + build_clusters_and_levels (imported by view-state) + the optional .mmd export.

write_levels writes per-level LN.mmd slices into the build's own out_dir/architecture-levels (cache-only), NOT into a target repo's docs/ tree. This satisfies both D001's 'cache-only, foreign-repo guarded' and the diffable-docs intent without risking mutation of a foreign project on a multi-repo build. The .mmd is never the render source: the page reads clusters/levels from the view-state. Best-effort in dashboard.build (a slice-write failure warns, never fails the build or blocks the view-state cache).

Reconciled the two divergent architecture_levels.py BEFORE merge (operator directive). 007's module is now the SINGLE source: cluster_key + build_clusters_and_levels define the only clustering, consumed by the view-state that drives the live interactive map. Folded the older 004/F008 Mermaid writer's render-truth + legibility mechanics IN BEHIND that model: compute_drift(snapshot, repo_root) (per-node drift from source_fingerprint.file_hashes), fresh/drift classDefs, pagination of dense clusters into <=25-node pages, ELK directive for busy levels. Canonical writer renamed write_levels -> export_mermaid_levels (drift overlay optional); write_levels kept as a thin alias. Dropped the old module's SECOND clustering (_clusters/_cluster_edges/separate cluster_key) and its hand-curated C4 L0-context/L1-lanes taxonomy — superseded by the directory-depth cluster/level model. The older generator had NO production call site (wired only into its own test_architecture_levels_f008.py), so no live caller was repointed. ON MERGE of the 004 branch: take 007's architecture_levels.py wholesale; delete the superseded test_architecture_levels_f008.py; if a docs-regen .mmd surface is later wired, call export_mermaid_levels(build_view_state(load_inputs(root)), out_dir=<docs/cache>, drift=compute_drift(snapshot, root)). Real build verified: 5 slices, 55 drifted files colored. 361 architecture/dashboard py tests green.
